name: Neustift im Stubaital
kurzbeschreibung: The largest village in the Stubaital, featuring mountain railways, glaciers, and family-friendly hiking trails.
text:
Overview

Neustift im Stubaital is located in the upper reaches of the Stubai Valley, approximately 25 kilometers south of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck at an altitude of 994 meters. Covering an expansive territory of 249 square kilometers, Neustift is the largest municipality by area in the Stubaital and the second-largest in all of Tyrol after Sölden. Alongside the bustling main village of Neustift-Dorf, the community encompasses numerous picturesque hamlets including Kampl, Neder, Milders, Krößbach, Gasteig, Volderau, Ranalt, and Mutterberg at the base of the glacier lift. The municipal borders reach up to the summit of the Zuckerhütl at 3,505 meters, the highest peak in the Stubai Alps. Neustift is globally renowned as a premier year-round alpine destination, framed by over 100 three-thousand-meter peaks and granting direct access to Austria's largest glacier ski resort.

History

Human presence in the Stubaital dates back to antiquity, with the valley name first recorded around the year 1000 as 'Stupeia'. Neustift itself was documented in the 14th century as 'Niwenstift' (new foundation). In the 16th century, Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian I regularly visited the upper valley for chamois and stag hunting, endowing a first chapel here in 1505. An architectural masterpiece is the monumental parish church of St. George, constructed between 1768 and 1774 according to the designs of celebrated Tyrolean builder-priest Franz de Paula Penz; ranking as the second-largest village church in Tyrol, it boasts magnificent Rococo ceiling frescoes by Franz Anton Zeiller. The historic churchyard holds the grave of the 'Glacier Priest' Franz Senn (1831–1884), a co-founder of the German Alpine Club in 1869 who pioneered alpine tourism in the Eastern Alps.

Getting There

Reaching Neustift is rapid and convenient due to its proximity to Innsbruck. Motorists take the A13 Brenner Autobahn to exit Schönberg/Stubaital and follow the well-paved B183 Stubaitalstraße up the valley for roughly 20 kilometers directly into Neustift (about 25 minutes from Innsbruck). A toll-free driving alternative uses the B182 Brenner road to Schönberg. Train passengers arrive at Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, where regular direct buses (VVT route 590 Stubaitalbus) operate every 30 minutes straight through Neustift-Dorf to the glacier terminal at Mutterberg. Valley bus transit is free for overnight visitors carrying the local Stubai Guest Card.

Tips

The foremost attraction is the Stubai Glacier, Austria's largest glacier ski resort offering guaranteed snow conditions up to 3,210 meters, the dramatic 360-degree 'Top of Tyrol' viewing platform, and an ice grotto carved deep inside ancient glacial ice. Starting right in the village, the Elferbahnen lift accesses Mount Elfer, featuring the world's largest walkable wooden sundial, a prime European paragliding launch, and two eight-kilometer natural toboggan runs illuminated for night sledding. Outdoor enthusiasts should hike the WildeWasserWeg trail to marvel at the 85-meter-wide Grawa Waterfall, celebrated for the therapeutic health benefits of its water aerosols. For avid trekkers, Neustift serves as the gateway to the world-famous Stubai High Trail traversing eight mountain huts around the valley.
